newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin fine, works for three hours-press service.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin fine, works for three hours-press service.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, who underwent open heart surgery 10 days ago, is recovering well and on Friday spent three hours working on official papers, his doctors said.

In their regular health bulletin on the 65-year-old president, published by the Kremlin press office, they said his condition remained "completely satisfactory", with a steady pulse of 70 to 82 beats a minute and normal temperature and blood pressure.
Earlier his press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing: "All indicators are stable. His movements are being expanded."
His aides are looking for the best time to stage Yeltsin's first appearence since his quintuple bypass operation, he said.
Yastrzhembsky said a planned address to the nation, Yeltsin's first public act, was still being prepared but he did not say when it would be.
On Tuesday Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin would address the nation within days, but did not specify whether it would be on television or radio.
On Friday he said no timetable for an address had been set but added that this had nothing to do with the president's state of health.
"You understand, the imagemakers want the president's appearance to have a big impact," he said.

He said that doctors, generally encouraged by the president's smooth progress, still wanted Yeltsin to build up his work-day step by step to avoid the risk of long-term damage to his health if he proceeds too quickly.
"The doctors favour progress achieved in small steps," Yastrzhembsky said.
"In the near future there are no meetings planned in his schedule," he said.

Pioneering U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey, who was a consultant during the operation, has said Yeltsin has good chances for unlimited activity in the next 10 or 15 years but has cautioned the president not to try to go too fast.
